# TherapyLog

> TherapyLog is a web-based TRT (testosterone replacement therapy) and peptide
> tracker for adults. It logs doses, models estimated serum levels from published
> half-lives, plans multi-compound syringe draws with compatibility rules, and
> tracks bloodwork against the reference range printed on the user's own lab
> report. Health data stays on the user's device. Free tier, no account required.

Site: https://therapylog.app/
Publisher: TherapyLog LLC, Floresville, Texas, USA
Contact: hello@therapylog.app

Generated by scripts/build-pages.js — the page list below is the page list that
exists, not a roadmap.

Disambiguation: "Therapylog" is also the name of an unrelated school-therapy
documentation product at therapylog.com. This is a different product. This one is
at therapylog.app and is a hormone-therapy and peptide tracker.

## Author and editorial policy

All reference content is written by Joel Gonzales, founder of TherapyLog. He is
not a clinician, and the site states that on every page. No clinical reviewer is
claimed. Claims cite primary literature or guideline documents; evidence is
labelled in three tiers (established clinical use, off-label or community
practice, animal-only or theoretical); the reference range printed on a user's
own lab report takes precedence over any generic range shown; optimal bands are
labelled non-diagnostic; every side-effect discussion ends with taking the result
to the prescribing clinician. The site sells software only, lists no vendor on
any reference page, and takes no referral fee from any clinic, pharmacy or
laboratory.

- /about/: Author, editorial policy, corrections process, what the site earns
  from, and what the tools do and do not do.

## Free calculators

Every calculator runs the app's own function source, lifted from the app when the
page is built and compared against it in continuous integration, so a page and
the app cannot disagree about a number. All are free and need no account.

- /tools/: Free calculators for injectable protocols — Reconstitution, syringe units, half-life and steady-state calculators that run the same code as the TherapyLog app. Free, no account, no email.

- /tools/peptide-reconstitution-calculator/: Peptide reconstitution calculator — Work out the bacteriostatic water to add and the units to draw — or start from the dose you want and solve backwards. Free, no account, same code as the app.
- /tools/insulin-syringe-units-calculator/: Insulin syringe unit converter — Units to ml and back on U-100 syringes, plus dose-to-units for any concentration. U-100 means 100 units per ml. Free, no account.
- /tools/trt-dose-calculator/: Testosterone dose calculator — Split a weekly testosterone dose by injection frequency — mg, ml and syringe units — with the modelled peak-to-trough swing per ester and cadence. Free, no account.
- /tools/free-testosterone-calculator/: Free testosterone calculator — Calculated free and bioavailable testosterone from total T, SHBG and albumin by the Vermeulen equation, in your lab’s units — and why the SHBG assay changes it.
- /tools/half-life-calculator/: Half-life and steady-state calculator — Half-life, time to steady state, accumulation ratio and peak-to-trough swing for 50 PK-modelled compounds. Free, no account.
- /tools/syringe-builder/: Combined syringe planner — Plan a multi-compound draw, see the stacked fill level, and get warned when compounds should not share a syringe: oil and water, suspensions, fragile proteins.
- /tools/stack-checker/: Can you take these together? — 45 documented interaction pairs across testosterone ancillaries, GLP-1 medications and peptides — the mechanism and what to watch. Free, no account.

### Reconstitution, pre-filled per compound

Each carries a milligram-to-units table computed for a stated vial and diluent
volume, the modelled half-life, and the storage rule.

- /tools/bpc-157-reconstitution-calculator/: BPC-157 reconstitution calculator

- /tools/semaglutide-reconstitution-calculator/: Semaglutide reconstitution calculator
- /tools/tb-500-reconstitution-calculator/: TB-500 reconstitution calculator
- /tools/tirzepatide-reconstitution-calculator/: Tirzepatide reconstitution calculator

### Pre-mixed multi-peptide blends

A blend vial holds several peptides dissolved in the same water, so one draw
takes all of them in the ratio the vial was compounded at. These pages compute
what a single draw delivers of each component and compare it against what the
literature and community practice describe for that compound on its own; the two
rarely match, because the ratio is fixed by whoever filled the vial. Ratios are
not standardised, so each page takes the numbers from the reader's own label.
The BPC-157 and TB-500 vial is widely known by the community nickname the
"Wolverine blend" or "Wolverine stack"; GLOW is GHK-Cu with BPC-157 and TB-500;
KLOW is GLOW with KPV added.

- /tools/bpc-157-tb-500-blend-calculator/: BPC-157 and TB-500 blend: what one draw actually delivers — What one draw of a Wolverine blend vial delivers of each component, and why a fixed ratio cannot match what each compound is dosed at on its own. Free, no account.
- /tools/glow-peptide-blend-calculator/: GLOW blend: what one draw actually delivers — What one draw of a GLOW vial delivers of each component, and why a fixed ratio cannot match what each compound is dosed at on its own. Free, no account.
- /tools/klow-peptide-blend-calculator/: KLOW blend: what one draw actually delivers — What one draw of a KLOW vial delivers of each component, and why a fixed ratio cannot match what each compound is dosed at on its own. Free, no account.

### Half-life and steady state, per compound

Each carries the single-dose and repeated-dose curves pre-rendered from the app's
own pkCurve function, the accumulation ratio, the time to steady state, the
peak-to-trough ratio, the monitoring panel, and the interaction rules naming that
compound. Estimated half-lives are labelled as estimates on every page they
appear on.

## Lab marker reference (/markers/)

Marker pages are written with the assay method named wherever it changes the
interpretation — sensitive (LC/MS-MS) versus standard immunoassay estradiol,
direct versus calculated versus equilibrium-dialysis free testosterone, and so
on. Each will carry the accepted units and their conversions, the generic
reference range labelled as generic, the non-diagnostic optimal band where one
exists, and authored explanation with primary sources. The hub at /markers/ lists
what is live; the fifteen markers being written are estradiol (sensitive versus
standard), total testosterone (immunoassay versus LC/MS-MS), free versus total
testosterone, SHBG, hematocrit on testosterone therapy, prolactin, LH and FSH,
IGF-1, HbA1c and fasting glucose, ApoB versus LDL, lipoprotein(a), ferritin and
the iron panel, vitamin D, the thyroid panel, and DHT.

## Lab marker reference

Written with the assay method named wherever it changes the interpretation —
sensitive (LC/MS-MS) versus standard immunoassay estradiol, direct versus
calculated versus equilibrium-dialysis free testosterone, and so on. Each page
carries the accepted units and their conversion factors, the assay variants the
app tracks, the generic reference range labelled as generic, the non-diagnostic
optimal band where one exists, the sex and age bands generated from the app's own
range function, a unit converter running the app's own conversion code, and cited
primary sources. The reference interval printed on the reader's own report always
takes precedence over any generic range shown.

- /markers/: Lab markers, read with the assay in mind — Reference pages for the lab markers people on hormone therapy and peptide protocols track, written with the assay method named wherever it changes the answer.

- /markers/apob-vs-ldl/: ApoB versus LDL cholesterol: counting particles instead of cargo — LDL-C measures cholesterol carried; ApoB counts the particles carrying it. Why they disagree, which LDL calculation your lab used, and what changes on testosterone or a GLP-1.
- /markers/estradiol-sensitive-vs-standard/: Sensitive versus standard estradiol: why the assay changes the answer — Standard estradiol immunoassays are unreliable at the concentrations men run. What the sensitive and LC/MS-MS methods measure, how to read the number, and why a range quoted without a method is not usable.
- /markers/free-vs-total-testosterone/: Free versus total testosterone, and the three ways labs get the free number — Calculated, direct immunoassay and equilibrium dialysis free testosterone are three different measurements. What each one does, why they disagree, and where SHBG comes in.
- /markers/hba1c-and-fasting-glucose/: HbA1c and fasting glucose: the conversion, and why donating blood distorts one of them — How mmol/mol converts to percent, what fasting glucose and insulin add, and why anything that shortens red cell lifespan — phlebotomy included — biases HbA1c low.
- /markers/hematocrit-on-trt/: Hematocrit on testosterone therapy: the thresholds, the trend, and the ferritin trap — Testosterone raises hematocrit. What the guideline thresholds are, why the draw conditions matter, and why routine blood donation trades one problem for iron deficiency.
- /markers/igf-1/: IGF-1: why the range is age-banded, and what secretagogues do to it — IGF-1 cannot be read without an age. What the age bands are, why assay standardisation matters, and what growth hormone secretagogues actually move.
- /markers/lh-fsh/: LH and FSH: what they show during suppression and during recovery — LH and FSH are the two markers that show whether your own production is running. What they do on testosterone therapy, what recovery looks like on paper, and why timing decides the result.
- /markers/prolactin/: Prolactin: what actually raises it, and what one high draw does not mean — Prolactin is easy to elevate by accident and easy to over-treat. What raises it, why a single high value is usually repeated before anything is done, and how the units differ.
- /markers/shbg/: SHBG: what it does, what raises and lowers it, and why it drives your free testosterone — Sex hormone-binding globulin decides how much of your testosterone is available. What raises and lowers it, why high SHBG on TRT is a common complaint, and how to read it.
- /markers/total-testosterone-immunoassay-vs-lcms/: Total testosterone: immunoassay versus LC/MS-MS, and the range by age — Why two labs report different total testosterone from the same blood, what the reference range does with age, and how to read a result when the method is not stated.
- /markers/trt-bloodwork-checklist/: The bloodwork checklist: which markers, which assay, when to draw — Which markers to order, which assay to specify, what context to record beside each result, and how often to draw. Generated from the app’s own marker registry.

## Disclaimer

TherapyLog is an informational tracking tool and is not a substitute for
professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. It does not diagnose, treat,
prescribe or monitor anyone. Calculators do the arithmetic entered into them and
nothing else; vial strength and diluent volume must be confirmed on the user's own
label. Serum-level curves are modelled estimates from published half-lives, not
measurements, and where the underlying half-life is itself an estimate the page
says so. It is for adults; the app requires an 18-or-older attestation.
Always consult a qualified healthcare provider before starting, changing, or
stopping any medical protocol.
